newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong people unfazed by handover to China-poll.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong people unfazed by handover to China-poll.

text.p: A poll conducted by the University of Hong Kong shows most people in the British colony are unfazed by the impending handover to China.
"The most frequent phrase used to describe their feeling towards the transition was 'no special feeling'," the survey, published on Thursday, concluded.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
The poll of 520 people conducted on December 31 showed most would choose to stay and many were willing to invest in the long-term future of Hong Kong.
Asked whether they would choose to stay or leave Hong Kong given a free choice, 80 percent plumped for remaining and only 17 percent said they would leave.

Some 38 percent of those surveyed chose neutral expressions to describe their feelings about the impending handover, 30 percent chose positive terms, including "happy" and "expectant", while only 15 percent described their feelings in negative terms, the survey carried out by the University's Social Science Research Centre, said.

The survey also concluded that 59 percent of respondents did not expect the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping to trigger turmoil in China, while 33 percent were worried that trouble would break out.
The approval rating of the 28th and last British Governor, Chris Patten, remained high -- at 58.5 percent in December against 58.4 percent in November.
His successor after the handover, shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, saw his high popularity rating decrease a shade.

Tung's rating averaged 67 percent in November, before he was chosen by a China-selected committee as the man to step into Patten's shoes on July 1, and averaged 66.3 percent after he was anointed Chief Executive-designate.
